title: Standings groups by raw team name, not the normalized team-key used everywhere else
evidence: src/brazilian_soccer_mcp/core.clj:114 uses (add (:home m) ...) / (add (:away m) ...) — the raw name strings — as the standings table key, whereas match? (core.clj:66-72), record-for (:78-86), team-stats and head-to-head all key on the normalized :home-key/:away-key. The bug is even encoded in the unit test: core_test.clj:21 seeds :home "Flamengo-RJ" and (other row) :away "Flamengo", so Flamengo is split into two 1-game standings rows and the test only checks the first is "Flamengo-RJ". Runtime effect (_factual.json): 2019 Serie A returned 21 rows with 3 Atletico/Athletico rows instead of 2 — Athletico Paranaense split into a 27-game row and an 11-game row (27+11=38) rather than one 38-game club; factual_accuracy=0.5.
suggestion: Key the standings map on (team-key team) like the rest of the code (or on :home-key/:away-key), carrying a display name separately, so state-suffix and accent variants collapse to one row per club.
